q: What is the commonest type of TOF?
o: Proximal oesophageal atresia with distal fistula (Gross type C)
why: Type C makes up most cases.

q: What is the classic postnatal finding?
o: Inability to pass an NG tube, which coils in the upper pouch on CXR
why: With excess salivation and choking on feeds.

q: Which association should be looked for?
why: Up to half have an associated anomaly; echo for cardiac lesions.

q: Why is bag-mask ventilation avoided before intubation?
o: Gas passes through the fistula and distends the stomach

q: Where should the ETT tip ideally sit?
o: Distal to the fistula (above the carina)
In the right main bronchus always
why: A bronchoscopy helps locate the fistula.

q: What is the purpose of a Replogle tube?
o: Continuous low-pressure suction of the upper pouch

q: What is the commonest post-op complication?
why: Also anastomotic leak, stricture and tracheomalacia.

q: When is TOF repair usually done?
What is a key anaesthetic immediate complication?
why: Also gastric distension and hypoxia during retraction.

q: Which gas is avoided in TOF repair?
why: N2O expands gas in the stomach.
